params.prompt: The insurer studies mortality: the expected pattern of deaths in the insured group. Interest assumptions reflect earnings on funds held before benefits are paid. Expenses include the costs of acquiring, administering and servicing the business, with appropriate pricing provisions. Holding other assumptions constant, higher expected mortality tends to increase the cost of death protection. Higher assumed interest can reduce the amount that must be collected now for the same future benefit. Greater expense needs increase the gross price. These are pricing relationships, not promises that the premium on an existing policy changes whenever market conditions move.
